To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BRCA1-defective ovarian carcinoma cells exhibit increased sensitivity and expression of the p53 family member TAp73, which is mediated by the loss of ZEB1-mediated repression of p73 expression through DNA hypermethylation of a ZEB1 binding motif.
BRCA1-deficent ovarian carcinoma cells are sensitive to cisplatin chemotherapy and this chemosensitivity is mediated through the epigenetic upregulation of p73.
BRCA1-associated epigentic regulation of p73, through ZEB1 binding, mediates an effctor pathway for chemosensitvity in ovarian carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate chemosensitivity and chemoresistance in BRCA1-related ovarian cancer.
understanding mechanisms of drug resistance in ovarian cancer, with the aim of developing novel therapies to improve outcomes in this disease.
the molecular mechanisms of ovarian carcinoma and how these mechanisms affect response to therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BRCA1-deficiency is associated with increased TAp73 expression through an epigenetic mechanism, which is important in the chemosensitivity of BRCA1-mutated ovarian carcinomas.
BRCA1-defective cells have increased sensitivity to cis-diamminedichloroplatinum (CDDP), or cisplatin, a chemotherapeutic drug.

BRCA1 deficiency in ovarian carcinoma cells is associated with hypermethylation of a regulatory region within the p73 gene, which includes the ZEB1-binding site, leading to the loss of ZEB1-mediated transcriptional repression and upregulation of TAp73.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have discovered a novel mechanism of chemosensitivity in a subset of cancers, which is mediated by the p53-related protein p73 and which is regulated by BRCA1.
BRCA1-defective ovarian carcinoma cells exhibit a novel epigenetically regulated pathway for p73 upregulation, and TAp73 is a mediator of the chemosensitivity of BRCA1-deficiency.
BRCA1-deficiency leads to hypermethylation of a p73 regulatory site, which leads to increased TAp73 expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BRCA1-associated epidermal growth factor receptor 1 (BRCA1-associated E3 ubiquitin ligase 1, also known as BARD1) protein complex is a tumor suppressor.
the BRCA1 protein is required for the maintenance of the DNA repair machinery in normal cells and in BRCA1-mutant cancer cells.
the BRCA1 tumor suppressor gene is a master regulator of p73, a p53-related gene, and that p73 mediates a pathway for chemosensitive response to DNA damage in BRCA1-mutated ovarian cancers.
